Synopsis:
Global equities and bonds rallied modestly while the yen surged ahead of key US data. The primary market driver is Friday's US payrolls report and Fed rate decision expectations. Money markets price a ~60% chance of a Fed hike this month (up sharply from <40% a week prior). US 10Y yields eased slightly to 4.766% after recent multi-year highs. Oil pulled back to ~$95 as US-Iran military strikes escalated. Gold surged to $4,436, up ~13% from June lows on USD debasement fears and geopolitical risk. The Dutch central bank relocated gold reserves from North America to London as a crisis hedge.
